script.title: Price Elasticity of Demand
script.caption_hook: Why does petrol use barely drop when the price rises? Price elasticity explains it.

lines.say: Why does the quantity of petrol demanded barely drop when price rises?
Good question! That's price elasticity of demand: how much buyers react to a price change.
So how do we measure that reaction?
Compare two percentages: percentage change in quantity demanded divided by percentage change in price.
Sure. A pen costs ₹10 and you buy 100. Price rises to ₹11. Now you buy 80.
So price rose 10%, and quantity fell 20%, right?
Exactly. Divide 20% by 10%. Ignoring the minus sign, the magnitude is 2.
Compare with 1. Above 1 is elastic: big reaction. Below 1 is inelastic. Exactly 1 is unitary.
Oh! So petrol must be inelastic, since people need it?
Yes, necessities are inelastic. Now revenue: for our elastic pen, the price rise cut revenue from ₹1,000 to ₹880.
So with inelastic demand, a price rise increases revenue?
Yes, when price rises. Elastic buyers escape, inelastic buyers stay stuck. Exactly 1 keeps revenue the same.
